source_text: V. Martianus ait: Quod discere semper optabam, repente confessus es errorem vestrae persuasionis et legis. habet ergo, ut dicis, filium deus? respondit Achatius: Habet. Martianus ait: Quis est filius dei? respondit Achatius: Verbum veritatis et gratiae. Martianus ait: Hoc habet nomen? respondit Achatius: Non de nomine interrogaveras, sed de ipsa filii potestate. Martianus ait: Nomen explana. sanctus Achatius respondit: Iesus Christus vocatur. Martianus ait: Ex qua dei uxore conceptus est? respondit sanctus Achatius: Non hominum more deus filium ex muliebri coitu genuit, sed Adam primum dextera sua faciente formavit. nam absit ut tu maiestati divinae contactum puellae mortalis affirmes. luto primi hominis membra composuit, et ubi integram iam compleverat effigiem, animam spiritumque concessit. sic et filius dei verbum veritatis ex dei corde processit. ideo scriptum est: Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum. Martianus ait: Corporalis igitur deus est? Achatius dixit: Ipse solus agnoscit, nos vero non cognoscimus invisibilem formam, sed virtutem potentiamque veneramur. Martianus ait: Si in corpore non est, etiam cordis ignarus est. nam sensus non potest esse sine membris. respondit Achatius: Non in his membris sapientia nascitur, sed a deo datur. quid ergo pertinet corpus ad sensum? Martianus ait: Cataphryges aspice, homines religionis antiquae, ad mea sacra conversos reliquisse quae fuerant, et nobiscum diis vota persolvere: et tu similiter parere festina. omnes catholicae legis collige Christianos et cum his religionem nostri imperatoris attende. veniat tecum omnis populus, ex tuo pendet arbitrio: respondit Achatius: Illi omnes non meo nutu, sed dei praecepto reguntur. audiant me itaque, si iusta persuadeam; sin vero perversa et nocitura, contemnant.
thought_title: The Son as Word from the Heart
orientation: Martianus questions Achatius about the Son of God and then orders him to gather the Christians of the whole church to follow the emperor religion.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus said: What I always desired to learn, you have suddenly confessed, the error of your persuasion and faith. Has God therefore, as you say, a son? Achatius answered: He has. Martianus said: Who is the Son of God? Achatius answered: Word of truth and of grace. Martianus said: Does he have this as name? Achatius answered: You had not asked about the name, but about the very power of the Son. Martianus said: Explain the name. Holy Achatius answered: He is called Jesus Christ. Martianus said: From which wife of God was he conceived? Holy Achatius answered: Not in the manner of men did God beget the son from intercourse with a woman, but he formed Adam the first with his right hand acting. For may it be far that you affirm contact with a mortal girl of the divine majesty. From mud he put together the limbs of the first man, and when he had already completed the whole image, he granted soul and spirit. Thus also the Son of God as Word of truth came forth from the heart of God. Therefore it is written: My heart has poured forth a good word. Martianus said: Is God therefore bodily? Achatius said: He alone knows, but we do not know the invisible form, but we venerate his power and might. Martianus said: If he is not in a body, he is also ignorant of heart. For sense cannot exist without limbs. Achatius answered: Wisdom is not born in these limbs, but is given by God. What therefore does body have to do with sense? Martianus said: Look at the Cataphrygians, men of ancient religion, turned to my rites to have left what they had been, and with us to pay vows to the gods: and you likewise hasten to obey. Gather all Christians of the whole church and with them observe the religion of our emperor. Let all the people come with you, it hangs from your judgment. Achatius answered: All those are ruled not by my nod, but by the command of God. Let them therefore hear me, if I persuade just things; but if perverse and harmful things, let them despise me.

pass_b_english: Martianus said, "What I have always wanted to learn, you have suddenly confessed: the error of your belief and law. So God has a Son, as you say?" Achatius answered, "He has." Martianus said, "Who is the Son of God?" Achatius answered, "The Word of truth and grace." Martianus said, "Does he have this as his name?" Achatius answered, "You had asked not about his name, but about the power of the Son himself." Martianus said, "Make the name plain." Saint Achatius answered, "He is called Jesus Christ."

Martianus said, "From which wife of God was he conceived?" Saint Achatius answered, "God did not beget his Son by intercourse with a woman, in the manner of men. He formed Adam first, with his right hand fashioning him. Far be it from you to ascribe the touch of a mortal girl to the divine majesty. He put together the limbs of the first man from mud, and when he had already completed the whole figure, he granted him soul and spirit. In the same way the Son of God, the Word of truth, came forth from the heart of God. For this reason it is written: My heart pours out a good word (Psalms 45:1)."

Martianus said, "So God is bodily?" Achatius said, "He alone knows that. We do not know his invisible form, but we revere his strength and power." Martianus said, "If he is not in a body, he also knows nothing of a heart. For sense cannot exist without limbs." Achatius answered, "Wisdom is not born in these limbs, but it is given by God. What, then, does the body have to do with sense?"

Martianus said, "Look at the Cataphrygians, men of an ancient religion. They have turned to my rites, abandoned what they were, and with us they pay their vows to the gods. Be quick to obey in the same way. Gather the Christians of the whole church, and with them observe the religion of our emperor. Let the whole people come with you; it hangs upon your decision." Achatius answered, "They are all ruled not by my nod, but by the command of God. So let them listen to me if I persuade them of what is just, but if it is perverse and harmful, let them refuse me."
